transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-24 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~45 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Atlas Head of Platform), Sofia Martinez (Atlas ML Eng), Kenji Tanaka (Atlas Security), Alicia Gomez (Atlas Product)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can start. Quick agenda — model selection, pinning, and fallbacks, plus any security asks.
[00:18] Ravi Patel: Yeah thanks Maya. We looked at the sheet you sent, some initial numbers look good. We're mostly concerned about p95 latency under load and cost per 1k tokens because of our high-volume summaries.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: Totally. So to orient — last week we ran two model variants: an 8-bit quantized variant of Redwood-xxl and a float16 open model. The quantized one saved about 25% in token cost but p95 moved up by ~40ms on our 2k context tests.
[00:52] Sofia Martinez: Just to flag, our latency SLO is 450ms p95. The quantized variant hit ~420ms but under burst it went to 520ms. Is that expected?
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: Mm-hmm, yeah that's the tail behavior we saw. Part of it is warm vs cold KV cache — prefix cache helps a lot. We can pin a warmed route to avoid cold-start penalties in the pilot.
[01:27] Kenji Tanaka: Quick sec — on the private side, if we go VPC/private deploy we need KMS integration and audit logs shipped to our SIEM. Is that supported in the POC?
[01:41] Maya Chen: Yes, we have KMS integrations and exportable audit logs. For POC we can provide a limited control plane access and we have a checklist doc, I'll share the link.
[01:54] Ravi Patel: Great. Back to models — we were comparing Redwood-xxl-8q, Redwood-large-fp16, and a smaller open model from the catalog. We want to pin one for the pilot but have a fallback path to a cheaper variant if capacity or latency degrades.
[02:11] Liam O'Connor: That aligns with recommended pattern — pin the target model for the route, define a fallback policy to an adjacent variant (e.g., Redwood-xxl-8q -> Redwood-large-fp16) and set automatic rollback triggers like sustained p95 > SLO or error rate increase.
[02:28] Alicia Gomez: How deterministic are the rollback triggers? We don't want noisy flips.
[02:35] Liam O'Connor: We recommend hysteresis: 3-minute sustained violation at p95, plus error delta > 2x baseline, and a cool-down of 10 minutes before reattempt. Also, canary traffic split to monitor.
[02:50] Maya Chen: We'll include an example rollout policy in the docs.
[02:56] Speaker 6: (unintelligible)
[03:05] Sofia Martinez: On the catalog comparison, one thing we noticed — the names in the sheet sometimes don't match the names in our infra. e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' got transcribed as 'Redwood Dedica' in the doc we downloaded — small but causes confusion when we script.
[03:22] Maya Chen: Good catch, sorry about that, I'll correct the labels in the catalog sheet.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: About cost — if we pin to Redwood-xxl-8q and we get steady traffic, what's the expected cost difference vs the fp16 variant? You mentioned ~25% savings but then increased latency. Can you quantify per 100k tokens?
[03:48] Liam O'Connor: Sure, ballpark from the run: fp16 was about $X per 100k tokens in our staging rates, 8q was about 0.75x that — so ~25% lower. I'll put exact numbers in the updated benchmark sheet. Note that batching/caching can change effective per-token cost significantly.
[04:06] Kenji Tanaka: Also need to confirm data retention policies for logs, and whether Redwood will persist prompt content in the hosted flow.
[04:17] Maya Chen: For hosted flows we retain transient logs for X days in the POC by default; for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention or disable storage. We'll send the retention/security matrix.
[04:30] Ravi Patel: For the pilot we probably want Dedicated or VPC to avoid sending prompts to shared storage. What are the timeline and steps to move to a private deployment?
[04:42] Liam O'Connor: For VPC we can provision a private control plane; typically 2-3 weeks for basic setup plus KMS integration depending on approval cycles. For a POC you can run a temporary dedicated pool with reserved capacity for the pilot.
[04:58] Sofia Martinez: One more technical — does KV cache persist across requests for multi-turn summarization? We want to avoid recomputing the whole context each time.
[05:10] Liam O'Connor: Yes, the runtime handles KV cache, and with pinned model variants we can keep warm cache between requests. If you have sticky routing we can ensure requests for a session hit the same pool to maximize cache hits.
[05:30] Ravi Patel: On the benchmarking, can you run the same prompt set but at our traffic distribution (80% short, 20% long) and include tokenization overhead?
[05:41] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. Please share the prompt sets and distribution and we'll replicate. Also consider tokenization difference between fp16 and 8q is negligible — performance differences are runtime/compute bound.
[05:58] Alicia Gomez: Regarding monitoring — what dashboards are available for token-level cost breakdowns and per-route p95?
[06:07] Maya Chen: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, and trace hooks. We can provision read-only access to your team for the pilot.
[06:19] Ravi Patel: Can you also show us a sample of the rollback policy config? We want to plug it into our infra team's automation.
[06:28] Liam O'Connor: Yeah I'll attach a YAML example in the follow-up. It includes thresholds, canary weights, fallback mappings, and cooldowns.
[06:37] Sofia Martinez: A couple of practical notes — sometimes the model names in the API response are slightly different which breaks our CI parsing. Could you provide canonical model_id to use?
[06:48] Maya Chen: We'll share canonical IDs. We'll also include mapping between model friendly names and API model_id.
[06:55] Kenji Tanaka: Security-wise, we will need a SOC 2 attestation and confirmation that KMS keys are customer-managed in private deploys. Also want to confirm RBAC for the Console.
[07:08] Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II; for private you can bring your KMS and we support SSO/SAML and RBAC in the Console. We'll attach the security pack and a short checklist.
[07:22] Ravi Patel: On the fallback path, if the pinned model is down, does Redwood auto-switch with no dropped requests?
[07:29] Liam O'Connor: The platform can do automatic fallback with minimal retries; there's a small retry window. In practice we do a synchronous failover to the fallback variant for in-flight requests. We can also queue short bursts if you prefer to rate-limit.
[07:44] Alicia Gomez: We prefer no silent switches that change semantic behavior; can the Console alert on a fallback event?
[07:51] Maya Chen: Yes, fallbacks and rollbacks are logged as events and you can get alerts (Slack, pager, email).
[07:59] Sofia Martinez: Can we test fallback behavior under load? Like force a failure and verify rollback?
[08:06] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely — we recommend a controlled fault injection during the pilot. We'll help script the scenario.
[08:15] Ravi Patel: Ok great. Anything else on model selection? I'm leaning to pin Redwood-xxl-8q but with an fp16 fallback. We need the exact numbers to decide.
[08:25] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll send the updated benchmark and explicitly show p50/p95/p99 and cost per 100k tokens for both variants.
[08:34] Speaker 6: (mumble)
[08:40] Sofia Martinez: One more nuance — quantization sometimes affects hallucination rate on our data. Did you see any delta in QA tests?
[08:50] Liam O'Connor: Small sample we ran showed minimal perf delta on our eval set, but every prompt set is different. For pilot we should run your evals and flag quality regressions tied to prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can help with model/quant recommendations.
[09:08] Ravi Patel: Do you have a tool to run regression alerts on prompt sets?
[09:14] Maya Chen: Yep, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts. We'll show a quick deck.
[09:21] Kenji Tanaka: Regarding onboarding, who will be our first point of contact for infra integration?
[09:27] Maya Chen: Liam will be SE lead for infra integration; I'm your AE for commercial and coordination.
[09:34] Ravi Patel: Cool. For timeline, we'd like to pick and pin the model by next Tuesday and start a two-week pilot. Is that feasible?
[09:44] Liam O'Connor: Feasible — if you provide prompt sets and traffic distribution today/this week we can run the additional benches and have numbers by Monday/Tuesday.
[09:53] Maya Chen: Ok action items recap at the end, but quick note — I'll share the updated sheet and the security pack right after.
[10:01] -- Mid call interruptions and small talk --
[18:02] Liam O'Connor: (long run of technical notes) On the runtime side, we usually pick kernels based on sequence length distribution; if your 20% long tail grows we'll choose a different kernel which changes perf profile — I'll include kernel notes in the bench doc.
[24:45] Sofia Martinez: Are there any recommended autoscaling policies for sudden spikes? We saw a spike last quarter and had a lot of throttling.
[24:54] Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated we recommend a reserved baseline plus burst capacity; you can set autoscale targets on queue latency and CPU/GPU utilization. Also, smart routing helps route low-priority requests to cheaper variants.
[25:10] Ravi Patel: We'll need clear instructions for setting those policies.
[25:15] Maya Chen: We'll include recommended policies and a sample config.
[28:30] Ravi Patel: Any legal/procurement blockers for the pilot?
[28:35] Maya Chen: For the pilot you'll be under the standard POC terms; for enterprise we can scope longer SLAs. Kenji, we'll send the data processing addendum.
[28:48] Kenji Tanaka: Good. Please include KMS key rotation details.
[28:52] Maya Chen: Will do.
[31:05] Liam O'Connor: Quick note on observability — we can instrument traces for per-token timing. That helps correlate p95 spikes to specific prompt patterns.
[31:18] Sofia Martinez: That would be helpful.
[31:23] Liam O'Connor: Also recommended: sticky routing for sessions to maximize KV cache.
[31:30] Ravi Patel: Ok. Anything else?
[31:34] Alicia Gomez: No, just one ask — can you include a mapping for model behaviors so Product can evaluate UX impact of fallback? E.g., key differences in summarization fidelity between 8q and fp16.
[31:49] Maya Chen: We'll include a behavior matrix with sample outputs.
[31:56] Ravi Patel: Sweet. Let's recap next steps.
[32:05] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Maya: updated benchmark sheet, security pack, canonical model IDs (due 2026-03-26). 2) Liam: run 4k-context + traffic-distribution benchmarks and provide exact p50/p95/p99 and cost per 100k tokens (due 2026-03-27). 3) Sofia: share prompt sets and traffic distribution (due 2026-03-26). 4) Kenji: send compliance questions and confirm KMS/SAML details (due 2026-03-29). 5) Schedule rollback/canary deep-dive for 2026-03-31.
[32:34] Ravi Patel: That works. Thanks everyone.
[32:38] Maya Chen: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the sheet and links.
[32:43] -- Call ends --
